# Overview

**Module 6: Instability**

This module handles:

1. Reading the settings file: analysis ranges, groups, time, control samples, manual control lengths and exclusions
2. For every measure (each tract and each combined measure), every range and every sample: distribution statistics and modal peaks
3. Group control setpoints, and instability metrics relative to the sample's own setpoint and to its group control
4. All of the above per read and, when UMIs were used, per molecule
5. Comparing tracts (when more than one was measured): whether reads that changed in one tract also changed in the other

**Metric definitions.** Every metric compares each read (or molecule) in a range with a **setpoint**, a reference length for that sample and range (defined below the table). *d* = the read's length minus the setpoint, in repeat units; *n* = how many reads or molecules are in the range. Every column of `instability.xlsx`, with its units, is listed in the workbook's `definitions` sheet.

```{r metric_definitions, results='asis'}
kk <- paste(params$expansion_thresholds, collapse = " and ")
md <- data.frame(
  Metric = c("instability_index", "expansion_index, contraction_index", "mean_change_above_setpoint, mean_change_below_setpoint",
             "share_at_setpoint, share_above_setpoint, share_below_setpoint", sprintf("share_Kplus_above_setpoint, share_Kplus_below_setpoint (K = %s)", kk),
             "n_at_setpoint, n_above_setpoint, n_below_setpoint", "expansion_ratio, contraction_ratio",
             "modal_minus_setpoint, median_minus_setpoint, mean_minus_setpoint"),
  Definition = c("mean(<em>d</em>) &ndash; Lee et al. (2010); positive = longer than the setpoint on average",
                 "sum of the positive (negative) <em>d</em> divided by <em>n</em>, so that instability index = expansion index + contraction index",
                 "mean <em>d</em> among the reads longer (shorter) than the setpoint: how large a typical expansion (contraction) is. Called mean_expansion_size and mean_contraction_size before v3.1, and EI and CI in Duke 2.x",
                 "share of reads at the setpoint (within half a unit), above it, and below it. Called prop_at, prop_above, prop_below before v3.1",
                 "share of reads at least K repeat units above (below) the setpoint. Called prop_above_K, prop_below_K before v3.1",
                 "the same as counts of reads or molecules",
                 "reads above (below) &divide; reads at the setpoint. Kept for continuity, but its denominator is a single length, so it is noisy; <code>share_Kplus_above_setpoint</code> is the stable alternative",
                 "the sample's modal, median or mean length minus the setpoint. Called modal_diff, median_diff, mean_diff before v3.1"))
md$Metric <- vapply(strsplit(md$Metric, ", "), function(x) paste0("<code>", x, "</code>", collapse = ", "), character(1))
md$Metric <- gsub("</code> \\(K = ", " (K = ", md$Metric)
cat(knitr::kable(md, format = "html", escape = FALSE,
                 table.attr = 'class="table table-condensed" style="width:100%; table-layout:auto;"'))
```

The setpoint is the **`r params$control_setpoint_metric`**: the sample's own (`sample_relative`) or the `r params$control_aggregation_method` across its group's control samples (`control_relative`; selection: `r params$control_sample_selection`). `r if (params$use_manual_controls) "A manual control length in the settings file (manual_control_repeat_length) replaces the group control for that sample and range." else "Manual control lengths in the settings file are not used (use_manual_controls = FALSE); set it to TRUE to make them replace the group control."`

**Outputs:**

- `06_instability/instability.xlsx` – a `definitions` sheet (every column, what it means and its units), ranges, distribution statistics, peaks, controls, instability metrics, tract-comparison statistics
- `06_instability/plots/` – control setpoints, instability index by range, timecourses by group for every measure and range, tract-comparison plots

# Settings

```{r load}
.t <- proc.time()["elapsed"]
safe_load_module(file.path(params$dir_out, "module_data", "03_repeat_detection.RData"), 3)
measures <- module3_output$measures; primary <- module3_output$primary
units <- list(reads = module3_output$lengths[, .(file_stem, id = qname, measure, length)])
m4_path <- file.path(params$dir_out, "module_data", "04_umi.RData")
if (isTRUE(params$umi) && file.exists(m4_path)) {
  safe_load_module(m4_path, 4)
  units$molecules <- module4_output$molecule_lengths[, .(file_stem, id = molecule_id, measure, length)]
}
samples_in_data <- unique(units$reads$file_stem)
st <- load_settings(params$path_settings, samples_in_data)
settings <- st$used
range_table <- build_range_table(settings, measures$measure, primary)
timings["Load"] <- proc.time()["elapsed"] - .t
```

`r nrow(settings)` samples have settings and are analysed. `r if (length(st$missing)) sprintf("%d samples in the data have no settings row and are left out: %s.", length(st$missing), paste(head(st$missing, 5), collapse = ", ")) else "Every sample in the data has a settings row."` `r if (nrow(st$excluded)) sprintf("%d samples are marked exclude and are left out of every analysis.", nrow(st$excluded)) else ""` Units analysed: **`r paste(names(units), collapse = " and ")`**.

How each measure's ranges are defined: a measure with its own `analysis_ranges_<measure>` column uses ranges on its own scale; otherwise reads are selected by their **`r primary`** length using the primary ranges, and the metrics are calculated on that measure. The selection is not applied to the other measure's own length: in a `r primary` range of 40–50, a combined measure such as a sum can run above 50. Every length is in units of that measure's motif (a pentanucleotide tract in 5 bp units), and a combined measure whose tracts have motifs of different lengths is in bp.

```{r range_overview}
ro <- as.data.table(range_table)[, .(samples = uniqueN(file_stem), ranges = paste(unique(range_label), collapse = "; ")),
                                 by = .(measure, range_measure, range_name)]
dt_full(ro, caption = "Ranges by measure (range_measure = the length used to select the reads)")
```

## Experiment map

Each bubble is one combination of group and time, sized and labelled by the number of samples.

```{r experiment_map, fig.height=max(3, 0.35 * length(unique(settings$group)) + 2)}
has_group <- any(!is.na(settings$group)) && "group" %in% params$cohort_plot_by
has_time <- any(!is.na(settings$time)) && "time" %in% params$cohort_plot_by
# group_label is the key for group controls, so it always follows the settings
# group column; cohort_plot_by only changes how the plots are laid out
settings$group_label <- ifelse(is.na(settings$group), "ungrouped", settings$group)
em <- settings %>% dplyr::count(group_label, time)
p_map <- if (has_time) ggplot(em, aes(time, group_label, size = n)) + geom_point(colour = "steelblue", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), size = 3, colour = "white") + scale_size_continuous(range = c(4, 14), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Time", y = NULL, title = "Samples by group and time") + theme_bw() else
  ggplot(em, aes(n, group_label)) + geom_col(fill = "steelblue") + geom_text(aes(label = n), hjust = -0.3) +
  labs(x = "Samples", y = NULL, title = "Samples per group") + theme_bw()
print(p_map); save_plot(p_map, file.path(plots_dir, "experiment_map.png"), 10, max(3, 0.35 * length(unique(settings$group_label)) + 2))
```

# Distribution statistics

```{r distributions}
.t <- proc.time()["elapsed"]
wide <- lapply(units, function(u) dcast(u[file_stem %in% settings$file_stem], file_stem + id ~ measure, value.var = "length"))
rt_by_sample <- split(as.data.table(range_table), by = "file_stem")
select_values <- function(W, r) {
  rm <- W[[r$range_measure]]; v <- W[[r$measure]]
  if (is.null(rm) || is.null(v)) return(numeric(0))
  v <- v[!is.na(rm) & rm >= r$lo & rm <= r$hi]
  apply_floor(v[is.finite(v)], r$floor)
}
dist_list <- list(); peak_list <- list()
for (u in names(wide)) {
  Wsplit <- split(wide[[u]], by = "file_stem")
  res <- apply_fn(intersect(names(rt_by_sample), names(Wsplit)), function(s) {
    W <- Wsplit[[s]]; rr <- rt_by_sample[[s]]
    out <- vector("list", nrow(rr)); pk <- vector("list", nrow(rr))
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(rr))) {
      r <- rr[i]
      rm <- W[[r$range_measure]]
      n_total <- if (is.null(rm)) 0L else sum(!is.na(rm) & rm >= r$lo & rm <= r$hi)
      x <- select_values(W, r)
      out[[i]] <- data.frame(file_stem = s, unit = u, measure = r$measure, range_measure = r$range_measure,
                             analysis_range_name = r$range_name, range_label = r$range_label, n_total = n_total, distribution_stats(x))
      pk[[i]] <- data.frame(file_stem = s, unit = u, measure = r$measure, analysis_range_name = r$range_name,
                            find_modal_peaks(x, r$max_peaks, params$range_peak_span))
    }
    list(dist = rbindlist(out), peaks = rbindlist(pk))
  })
  dist_list[[u]] <- rbindlist(lapply(res, `[[`, "dist")); peak_list[[u]] <- rbindlist(lapply(res, `[[`, "peaks"))
}
distribution_summary <- rbindlist(dist_list); modal_peaks <- rbindlist(peak_list)
meta <- as.data.table(settings)[, .(file_stem, group, group_label, time, is_control)]
distribution_summary <- meta[distribution_summary, on = "file_stem"]
timings["Distributions"] <- proc.time()["elapsed"] - .t
```

## Reads and molecules in each range

Each point is one sample: how many reads (and molecules) fall in each range of the primary measure. Ranges with only a handful of reads per sample give unreliable metrics.

```{r range_counts, fig.height=5}
rc <- distribution_summary[measure == primary]
p_rc <- ggplot(rc, aes(analysis_range_name, pmax(n_total, 1), colour = unit)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, fill = NA, position = position_dodge(0.8)) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.15, dodge.width = 0.8), alpha = 0.6, size = 1.2) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = comma) + scale_colour_manual(values = unit_cols, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Analysis range", y = "Count in range (log scale)", title = paste("Reads and molecules per range:", primary)) +
  theme_bw() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
print(p_rc); save_plot(p_rc, file.path(plots_dir, "counts_per_range.png"), 11, 5)
```

# Group controls

**How the group controls are calculated.** Reads and molecules are handled separately, each from its own distribution statistics above:

1. **Which samples.** The control samples of each group are chosen by `control_sample_selection` = **`r params$control_sample_selection`** (`flagged`: the samples marked as controls in the settings file; `earliest`: the samples at the group's earliest time point; `all`: every sample in the group).
2. **One value per control sample.** For each control sample, unit (reads or molecules), measure and range, its **`r params$control_setpoint_metric`** is taken from all its reads (or all its molecules) in the range.
3. **One setpoint per group.** These values are combined across the group's control samples by the **`r params$control_aggregation_method`**, giving one setpoint for each group, unit, measure and range. `control_sd` is the spread between the control samples and `control_n` how many there are.

The read-based setpoint is used for read-based metrics, and the molecule-based setpoint for molecule-based metrics, so a sample is never compared with a control counted a different way. `r if (params$use_manual_controls) "Where the settings file gives a manual control length, it replaces this setpoint for that sample and range (for reads and molecules alike)." else ""`

```{r controls}
.t <- proc.time()["elapsed"]
sp_metric <- params$control_setpoint_metric
plot_ranges_c <- if (length(params$plot_ranges)) params$plot_ranges else head(sort(unique(range_table$range_name[range_table$measure == primary])), 2)
ctrl_pool <- distribution_summary[!is.na(get(sp_metric))]
if (params$control_sample_selection == "flagged") ctrl_pool <- ctrl_pool[is_control == TRUE]
if (params$control_sample_selection == "earliest") {
  if (!any(!is.na(distribution_summary$time))) stop("control_sample_selection = 'earliest' needs a time column in the settings file")
  ctrl_pool <- ctrl_pool[!is.na(time)][, .SD[time == min(time)], by = .(group_label, unit, measure, analysis_range_name)]
}
group_controls <- if (isTRUE(params$group_control) && nrow(ctrl_pool)) ctrl_pool[, .(
  control_setpoint = aggregate_controls(get(sp_metric), params$control_aggregation_method),
  control_sd = sd(get(sp_metric)), control_n = .N, control_samples = paste(file_stem, collapse = "; ")),
  by = .(group_label, unit, measure, analysis_range_name)] else data.table()
if (isTRUE(params$group_control) && nrow(group_controls) == 0)
  warning("No control samples found (selection: ", params$control_sample_selection, "). Only sample-relative metrics are calculated.")
timings["Controls"] <- proc.time()["elapsed"] - .t
if (nrow(group_controls)) dt_full(group_controls, caption = sprintf("Group control setpoints (%s of the controls' %s)", params$control_aggregation_method, sp_metric), digits = 2)
```

`r if (nrow(group_controls)) sprintf("**How to read this.** One panel per group, for %s in ranges %s. Each point is one control sample's %s, read-based (grey) and molecule-based (teal), and the horizontal bar is the group's setpoint, the %s of those points. Points close together mean the controls agree and the setpoint is well defined; a control far from the others pulls the setpoint and every control-relative metric of its group with it, so check it before trusting that group's results.", primary, paste(plot_ranges_c, collapse = ", "), gsub("_", " ", sp_metric), params$control_aggregation_method) else ""`

```{r control_plot, eval=nrow(group_controls) > 0, fig.height=4.5}
cp <- ctrl_pool[measure == primary & analysis_range_name %in% plot_ranges_c][, unit := factor(unit, levels = c("reads", "molecules"))]
gcp <- group_controls[measure == primary & analysis_range_name %in% plot_ranges_c]
if (nrow(cp)) {
  p_ctrl <- ggplot(cp, aes(unit, get(sp_metric), colour = unit)) +
    geom_crossbar(data = gcp, aes(y = control_setpoint, ymin = control_setpoint, ymax = control_setpoint), width = 0.6, colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_jitter(width = 0.12, height = 0, size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
    facet_grid(analysis_range_name ~ group_label, scales = "free_y", labeller = labeller(group_label = as_labeller(wrap_label))) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = unit_cols, guide = "none") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = paste("Control sample", gsub("_", " ", sp_metric)), title = paste("Control samples and group setpoints:", primary),
         subtitle = "Points = control samples; bar = the group setpoint") + theme_bw() + theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 7))
  print(p_ctrl); save_plot(p_ctrl, file.path(plots_dir, "control_setpoints.png"), min(40, 3 + 2.2 * uniqueN(cp$group_label)), 2 + 2.5 * length(plot_ranges_c))
}
```

# Instability metrics

```{r instability}
.t <- proc.time()["elapsed"]
setp <- distribution_summary[, .(file_stem, unit, measure, analysis_range_name, group_label, own = get(sp_metric))]
if (nrow(group_controls)) {
  setp <- group_controls[, .(group_label, unit, measure, analysis_range_name, control_setpoint, control_sd, control_n)][setp, on = .(group_label, unit, measure, analysis_range_name)]
} else setp[, `:=`(control_setpoint = NA_real_, control_sd = NA_real_, control_n = NA_integer_)]
manual <- as.data.table(range_table)[!is.na(manual_control) & isTRUE(params$use_manual_controls), .(file_stem, measure, analysis_range_name = range_name, manual_control)]
setp <- manual[setp, on = .(file_stem, measure, analysis_range_name)]
setp[, control_source := fifelse(!is.na(manual_control), "manual", fifelse(!is.na(control_setpoint), "group control", NA_character_))]
setp[!is.na(manual_control), `:=`(control_setpoint = manual_control, control_sd = NA_real_, control_n = NA_integer_)]
inst_list <- list()
for (u in names(wide)) {
  Wsplit <- split(wide[[u]], by = "file_stem")
  sp_u <- split(setp[unit == u], by = "file_stem")
  res <- apply_fn(intersect(names(rt_by_sample), names(Wsplit)), function(s) {
    W <- Wsplit[[s]]; rr <- rt_by_sample[[s]]; sp <- sp_u[[s]]
    out <- list()
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(rr))) {
      r <- rr[i]; x <- select_values(W, r)
      spi <- sp[measure == r$measure & analysis_range_name == r$range_name]
      for (type in c("sample_relative", "control_relative")) {
        s0 <- if (type == "sample_relative") spi$own[1] else spi$control_setpoint[1]
        if (!length(s0) || is.na(s0)) next
        out[[length(out) + 1]] <- data.frame(file_stem = s, unit = u, measure = r$measure, analysis_range_name = r$range_name,
          setpoint_type = type, setpoint_metric = sp_metric,
          setpoint_source = if (type == "sample_relative") "sample" else spi$control_source[1],
          instability_stats(x, s0, params$expansion_thresholds))
      }
    }
    rbindlist(out)
  })
  inst_list[[u]] <- rbindlist(res)
}
instability_metrics <- rbindlist(inst_list)
setnames(instability_metrics, "setpoint", "setpoint_length")
instability_metrics <- distribution_summary[, .(file_stem, unit, measure, analysis_range_name, group, group_label, time, is_control,
                                                modal_length, median_length, mean_length, sd)][instability_metrics, on = .(file_stem, unit, measure, analysis_range_name)]
instability_metrics[, `:=`(modal_minus_setpoint = modal_length - setpoint_length, median_minus_setpoint = median_length - setpoint_length,
                           mean_minus_setpoint = mean_length - setpoint_length)]
cz <- setp[, .(file_stem, unit, measure, analysis_range_name, own, control_setpoint, control_sd)]
instability_metrics <- cz[instability_metrics, on = .(file_stem, unit, measure, analysis_range_name)]
instability_metrics[setpoint_type == "control_relative" & control_sd > 0, z_score := (own - control_setpoint) / control_sd]
instability_metrics[, c("own", "control_setpoint", "control_sd") := NULL]
timings["Instability metrics"] <- proc.time()["elapsed"] - .t
```

## Timecourses by group

```{r headline_setup}
plot_ranges <- if (length(params$plot_ranges)) params$plot_ranges else head(sort(unique(range_table$range_name[range_table$measure == primary])), 2)
hl <- intersect(update_metric_names(params$headline_metrics), names(instability_metrics))
hl_type <- if (params$headline_setpoint_type %in% instability_metrics$setpoint_type) params$headline_setpoint_type else "sample_relative"
hl_labels <- c(modal_length = "Modal length", median_length = "Median length", mean_length = "Mean length",
               instability_index = "Instability index", expansion_index = "Expansion index", contraction_index = "Contraction index",
               mean_change_above_setpoint = "Mean change above\nthe setpoint", mean_change_below_setpoint = "Mean change below\nthe setpoint",
               expansion_ratio = "Expansion ratio",
               setNames(paste0("Share ", params$expansion_thresholds, "+ units\nabove the setpoint"), threshold_col(params$expansion_thresholds, "above")),
               setNames(paste0("Share ", params$expansion_thresholds, "+ units\nbelow the setpoint"), threshold_col(params$expansion_thresholds, "below")),
               share_above_setpoint = "Share above\nthe setpoint", share_below_setpoint = "Share below\nthe setpoint")
timecourse_plot <- function(d, title) {
  # One row per metric (each with its own y axis, % ticks for proportions), one column per group
  rows <- lapply(seq_along(hl), function(k) {
    v <- hl[k]; dd <- d[, .(time, group_label, unit, value = get(v))]
    is_prop <- grepl("^share", v)
    base <- if (has_time) ggplot(dd, aes(time, value, colour = unit)) + geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 1.6) +
        stat_summary(aes(group = unit), fun = mean, geom = "line", linewidth = 0.8)
      else ggplot(dd, aes(group_label, value, colour = unit)) + geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, fill = NA) +
        geom_jitter(width = 0.15, height = 0, alpha = 0.6)
    base + facet_wrap(~ group_label, nrow = 1, scales = if (has_time) "fixed" else "free_x") +
      scale_colour_manual(values = unit_cols, name = NULL, drop = TRUE) +
      (if (is_prop) scale_y_continuous(labels = pct_axis()) else scale_y_continuous()) +
      labs(x = if (k == length(hl)) (if (has_time) "Time" else NULL) else NULL, y = if (v %in% names(hl_labels)) hl_labels[[v]] else v) +
      theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = if (k == 1) "top" else "none",
                         strip.text = if (k == 1) element_text(size = 8) else element_blank(),
                         strip.background = if (k == 1) element_rect() else element_blank(),
                         axis.text.x = if (k == length(hl)) element_text() else element_blank())
  })
  patchwork::wrap_plots(rows, ncol = 1) + patchwork::plot_annotation(title = title,
    subtitle = sprintf("Points = samples; lines = mean at each time.\nInstability metrics %s; setpoint = %s.", gsub("_", " ", hl_type), gsub("_", " ", sp_metric)))
}
n_groups <- length(unique(instability_metrics$group_label))
tc_w <- min(40, 3 + 3.2 * n_groups); tc_h <- min(40, 1.9 * length(hl) + 2)
```

The headline metrics for each group, plotted against time: one column per group, one row per metric, each row on its own scale. Length metrics (modal, median, mean) are the sample's own; the instability metrics are `r gsub("_", " ", hl_type)`. Reads are grey`r if ("molecules" %in% names(units)) " and molecules teal" else ""`. Shown here: **`r primary`**, ranges `r paste(plot_ranges, collapse = ", ")`. Every measure and range is saved in `plots/timecourse/`.

```{r headline_plots, fig.width=tc_w, fig.height=tc_h, results='asis'}
.t <- proc.time()["elapsed"]
for (m in measures$measure) for (rg in sort(unique(range_table$range_name[range_table$measure == m]))) {
  d <- instability_metrics[measure == m & analysis_range_name == rg & setpoint_type == hl_type]
  if (!nrow(d)) next
  lab <- range_table$range_text[range_table$measure == m & range_table$range_name == rg][1]
  p <- timecourse_plot(d, sprintf("%s, %s (%s)", m, rg, lab))
  save_plot(p, file.path(plots_dir, "timecourse", safe_path(m), paste0(safe_path(m), "-", rg, ".png")), tc_w, tc_h)
  if (m == primary && rg %in% plot_ranges) { cat("\n\n### ", m, ", ", rg, " (", lab, ")\n\n", sep = ""); print(p) }
}
timings["Timecourse plots"] <- proc.time()["elapsed"] - .t
```

## Instability index across ranges

**How to read this.** The `r primary` instability index (`r gsub("_", " ", hl_type)`) of every sample in every range, one panel per group: the x-axis is the range (as defined in the settings file), each point one sample, read-based in grey and molecule-based in teal, with a box for the spread across samples. **What it shows.** How much the result depends on the range chosen. Where a range cuts through an allele's peak, or takes in a smear of short PCR products, its index moves away from the neighbouring ranges; a range that agrees with its neighbours, and where reads and molecules agree, is a safer headline.

```{r ii_by_range, fig.height=min(30, 1.5 + 3 * ceiling(uniqueN(instability_metrics$group_label) / 2))}
ir <- instability_metrics[measure == primary & setpoint_type == hl_type & !is.na(instability_index)]
if (nrow(ir)) {
  # One label per range; a range whose bounds differ between samples is labelled as such
  rlab <- as.data.table(range_table)[measure == primary, .(range_text = if (uniqueN(range_text) == 1) range_text[1] else "varies by sample"),
                                     by = .(analysis_range_name = range_name)]
  ir <- rlab[ir, on = "analysis_range_name"][, unit := factor(unit, levels = c("reads", "molecules"))]
  ir[, xlab := factor(paste0(analysis_range_name, "\n", range_text), levels = unique(paste0(rlab$analysis_range_name, "\n", rlab$range_text)[order(rlab$analysis_range_name)]))]
  p_ir <- ggplot(ir, aes(xlab, instability_index, colour = unit)) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, fill = NA, position = position_dodge(0.8)) +
    geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.15, dodge.width = 0.8), alpha = 0.5, size = 1) +
    facet_wrap(~ group_label, ncol = 2, labeller = as_labeller(wrap_label)) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = unit_cols, name = NULL) +
    labs(x = "Analysis range", y = "Instability index (units)", title = paste("Instability index by range:", primary),
         subtitle = paste("Each point is one sample;", gsub("_", " ", hl_type))) +
    theme_bw() + theme(axis.text.x = if (uniqueN(ir$analysis_range_name) > 6) element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, size = 7) else element_text(size = 8),
                       legend.position = "top")
  print(p_ir); save_plot(p_ir, file.path(plots_dir, "instability_index_by_range.png"), min(40, 4 + 0.7 * uniqueN(ir$analysis_range_name) * 2), min(40, 1.5 + 3 * ceiling(uniqueN(ir$group_label) / 2)))
}
```

```{r instability_table}
show_cols <- c("file_stem", "unit", "measure", "analysis_range_name", "group", "time", "setpoint_type", "setpoint_length",
               "n_used", "modal_length", "median_length", "mean_length", "instability_index", "expansion_index", "contraction_index",
               threshold_col(params$expansion_thresholds, "above"), "expansion_ratio", "z_score")
dt_full(instability_metrics[, intersect(show_cols, names(instability_metrics)), with = FALSE], caption = "Instability metrics (key columns; every column is in instability.xlsx)", digits = 3)
```

# Comparing tracts

When more than one tract is measured (for example CAG and CCG), this asks whether a read (or molecule) whose length changed in one tract also changed in the other – for example whether CAG instability carries the CCG tract with it. Pairs are set by `measure_pairs`; by default every pair of tracts is compared.

```{r pairs_setup}
tr_meas <- measures$measure[measures$type == "tract"]
pairs <- if (length(params$measure_pairs)) strsplit(params$measure_pairs, ":") else if (length(tr_meas) > 1) combn(tr_meas, 2, simplify = FALSE) else list()
has_pairs <- length(pairs) > 0
```

`r if (!has_pairs) "Only one tract was measured, so there is nothing to compare." else ""`

```{r pairs, eval=has_pairs, fig.height=5.5, results='asis'}
.t <- proc.time()["elapsed"]
pair_stats <- list(); pair_bins <- list()
for (pr in pairs) {
  A <- pr[1]; B <- pr[2]
  for (u in names(wide)) {
    W <- wide[[u]]
    if (!all(c(A, B) %in% names(W))) next
    for (rg in plot_ranges) {
      rr <- as.data.table(range_table)[measure == A & range_name == rg]
      if (!nrow(rr)) next
      d <- rr[, .(file_stem, range_measure, lo, hi)][W, on = "file_stem", nomatch = NULL]
      d <- d[!is.na(get(A)) & !is.na(get(B))]
      d <- d[get(unique(range_measure)[1]) >= lo & get(unique(range_measure)[1]) <= hi]
      if (!nrow(d)) next
      d[, `:=`(a = get(A), b = get(B))]
      d[, `:=`(dA = a - median(a), dB = b - median(b)), by = file_stem]
      ps <- d[, .(n = .N, rho = suppressWarnings(cor(a, b, method = "spearman")), median_A = median(a), median_B = median(b)), by = file_stem]
      ps[, `:=`(unit = u, measure_A = A, measure_B = B, analysis_range_name = rg)]
      pair_stats[[length(pair_stats) + 1]] <- ps
      d[, dA_bin := pmin(pmax(round(dA), -15), 15)]
      pb <- d[, .(mean_dB = mean(dB), n = .N), by = .(file_stem, dA_bin)][meta, on = "file_stem", nomatch = NULL]
      pb[, `:=`(unit = u, measure_A = A, measure_B = B, analysis_range_name = rg)]
      pair_bins[[length(pair_bins) + 1]] <- pb
      # per-sample scatter
      if (params$plot_per_sample) for (s in unique(d$file_stem)) {
        ds <- d[file_stem == s]; if (nrow(ds) > params$pair_max_points) { set.seed(123); ds <- ds[sample(.N, params$pair_max_points)] }
        p <- ggplot(ds, aes(a, b)) + geom_jitter(width = 0.25, height = 0.25, alpha = 0.3, size = 0.8) +
          labs(x = paste(A, "length"), y = paste(B, "length"), title = s, subtitle = sprintf("%s, %s, %s; each point = one %s, jittered by up to 0.25", u, rg, A, sub("s$", "", u))) + theme_bw()
        save_plot(p, file.path(plots_dir, "pairs", paste0(A, "_vs_", B), u, paste0(s, "-", rg, ".png")), 7, 6)
      }
    }
  }
}
pair_stats <- rbindlist(pair_stats); pair_bins <- rbindlist(pair_bins)
timings["Pairs"] <- proc.time()["elapsed"] - .t
for (pr in pairs) for (rg in plot_ranges) {
  A <- pr[1]; B <- pr[2]
  pb <- pair_bins[measure_A == A & measure_B == B & analysis_range_name == rg]
  if (!nrow(pb)) next
  cat(sprintf("\n\n### %s against %s, %s\n\n", B, A, rg))
  cat(sprintf("For each sample, every %s's change from the sample's median in **%s** (x, rounded, capped at ±15) against its change in **%s** (y). Each thin line is one sample; the thick line is the mean across samples in the group. A flat line at zero means %s does not change with %s; a rising line means reads that expanded in %s also lengthened in %s. Reads and molecules are drawn separately; read-level co-variation can partly reflect PCR and sequencing error on the same read.\n\n",
              "read or molecule", A, B, B, A, A, B))
  p <- ggplot(pb, aes(dA_bin, mean_dB, colour = unit)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_line(aes(group = interaction(file_stem, unit)), alpha = 0.25) +
    stat_summary(aes(group = unit), fun = mean, geom = "line", linewidth = 1.1) +
    facet_wrap(~ group_label) + scale_colour_manual(values = unit_cols, name = NULL) +
    labs(x = sprintf("Change in %s from the sample median", A), y = sprintf("Mean change in %s", B),
         title = sprintf("%s change against %s change, %s", B, A, rg)) + theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "top")
  print(p); save_plot(p, file.path(plots_dir, paste0("pair_", A, "_vs_", B, "_", rg, ".png")), 11, 5.5)
  ps <- pair_stats[measure_A == A & measure_B == B & analysis_range_name == rg][meta, on = "file_stem", nomatch = NULL]
  p2 <- ggplot(ps, aes(group_label, rho, colour = unit)) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, fill = NA, position = position_dodge(0.8)) +
    geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.15, dodge.width = 0.8), alpha = 0.7) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = unit_cols, name = NULL) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Spearman correlation", title = sprintf("Per-sample correlation of %s and %s lengths, %s", A, B, rg)) +
    theme_bw() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
  print(p2); save_plot(p2, file.path(plots_dir, paste0("pair_correlation_", A, "_vs_", B, "_", rg, ".png")), 10, 5)
}
```

# Save output

```{r save}
module6_output <- list(settings = settings, range_table = range_table, distribution_summary = distribution_summary, modal_peaks = modal_peaks,
                       group_controls = group_controls, instability_metrics = instability_metrics, 
                       pair_stats = if (has_pairs) pair_stats else NULL, pair_bins = if (has_pairs) pair_bins else NULL,
                       excluded = st$excluded, hash = params$module_hash)
output_path <- file.path(params$dir_out, "module_data", "06_instability.RData")
save(module6_output, file = output_path)
write_excel_function(list(definitions = metric_definitions(params$expansion_thresholds), range_table = range_table, distribution_summary = distribution_summary, modal_peaks = modal_peaks,
                          group_controls = group_controls, instability_metrics = instability_metrics, 
                          pair_stats = module6_output$pair_stats, excluded_samples = st$excluded), xlsx_path)
```
